newsitem.title: USA: PepsiCo faces woes with restaurant chains.
newsitem.headline: PepsiCo faces woes with restaurant chains.

text.p: Struggling to resolve problems with its bottling operations in Latin America, soft drink maker PepsiCo Inc also faces waning performances at its U.S. restaurant chains.

Industry analysts said PepsiCo's Taco Bell and Pizza Hut chains were not performing as well as expected. The chains, which represented 37 percent of revenues in 1995, were either slow at promoting themselves or introducing new products, they said.

Gary Black at Sanford C. Berstein said investor worries about the performance of the chains was hurting PepsiCo's stock, which fell 19 percent from 35 1/2 on June 28 to 28 5/8 on August 29. On Friday, it was trading at 28 3/4.
"The (stock price's) momentum is certainly on the down side," said Mitchell Pinheiro at Janney Montgomery Scott.
Roy Burry of Oppenheimer & Co said Taco Bell was having trouble after failing to introduce any new products.
Goldman downgraded it to moderate outperform, while Morgan cut its share earnings estimate to $1.38 from $1.40 for 1996, citing lowered expectations for its restaurant chains.
PepsiCo officials were not immediately available for comment.

PepsiCo's troubles began in early August when Buenos Aires Embotelladora SA (BAESA), its biggest bottler outside the United States, was reported to be struggling to turn around its losses and refinance $647 million of debt.
The Argentinian bottler, of which PepsiCo owns 24 percent, reported a loss of $251 million for the third quarter this year and expected more losses during the fourth.
PepsiCo then lost its sole bottler in Venezuela when Grupo Cisneros Embotelladoras Hit de Venezuela defected August 16 to the company's archrival, Coca Cola Co.
Traders began selling the stock on August 9, letting the price fall to 30 3/8 from 31 1/2.
"There's a continuing worry as to how big is the problem in Latin America," said Black, who said he expected the stock to come close to $25 in the short term.
But Terry Bivens at Donald & Co Securities said he remained optimistic. "These problems are imminently correctable," he said, adding that he still held a "buy" recommendation on the stock.
